# SPEC

## §G GOAL
Browser WebGPU node compositor: typed graph → compiled pass plan → live multi-branch preview, dark pro-tool UI, agent-drivable via 1 semantic command bus. Phase 0 + Phase 1 of `docs/vgpu-visual-node-compositor-implementation-handoff.md` only.

## §C CONSTRAINTS

### stack (locked)
- React 19 + TypeScript strict + Vite. pnpm.
- graph UI: `@xyflow/react`. presentation & gesture only.
- GPU: `vgpu` (vercel-labs), exact pinned version.
- state: `zustand` + `immer`. selective subscriptions.
- panes: `react-resizable-panels`. persisted layout.
- shader editor: CodeMirror 6 (⊥ Monaco — bundle size, theming to tokens).
- primitives: Radix UI, fully restyled.
- style: CSS vars + CSS modules. ⊥ Tailwind.
- validation: `zod`.
- test: `vitest` (unit + `vgpu/mock`), Dawn headless node render, `playwright` browser.
- persist: versioned JSON, ext `.loom.json`.

No fidelity changes or concurrent local GPU benchmarks. This remains static-source endurance, not animated latency or platform parity.

### point model — unified pointset (TD POP analog), Phase 2/3
ONE data model. mesh = points + topology. particles = points w/o topology. ⊥ SOP/POP split.
- storage = structure-of-arrays: 1 buffer per attribute. kills WGSL alignment pain; op binds only what it touches.
- arbitrary named attributes day 1. WGSL structs CODE-GENERATED from attribute schema.
- kernel ABI: `fn process(p: Point, ctx) -> Point`. `Point` codegen'd. versioned (`contractVersion`), fusion-ready.
- per-point RNG = `hash(seed, pointId, frame)`. `pointId` = identity, ⊥ slot index.
- GPU-driven lifecycle from start via scan/prefix-sum COMPACTION, ⊥ atomics — atomics ⊥ deterministic, would break V45 + headless parity. cost = 2-3 extra passes, nothing else.
- render spine: sprites → instances → mesh.
- TOP↔POP bridges: `TextureToAttribute` (P3a), splat-to-texture (P3b), audio/pointer via resolver seam (V61). one instrument, ⊥ two apps.

### three libraries, three verbs (TD: OP Create dialog | Palette | example projects)
- **node library** — a TYPE. verb = ADD. already exists.
- **component library** — a reusable subgraph (TD Palette / `.tox`). verb = INSTANTIATE into the
  current graph, linked or detached, at a pinned version (V79, V84). shipped set + user-saved.
- **example library** — a whole PROJECT. verb = OPEN, which REPLACES the open document.

⊥ merge into one browser. the verbs differ, and merging puts a DESTRUCTIVE action (open
replaces your work) one click from an additive one. examples ! confirm when the document
is dirty; add/instantiate ! never confirm — they are undoable.

shipped components (handoff §31.4, buildable w/ current catalogue):
FeedbackEcho · Bloom · DisplacementStack · MediaGrade · Kaleidoscope.

### media needs a resource kind that ⊥ exist yet
`ResourceDescriptor` = target | pingPong | sampler | buffer | bufferPair. **⊥ way to
carry a texture the CPU supplies.** ∀ current resource is GPU-allocated & GPU-written;
a decoded frame comes from outside. ∴ media is blocked on plan-IR work, ⊥ on node work —
worth knowing before anyone starts w/ the node.

```ts
interface ExternalTextureResourceDescriptor {
  kind: "externalTexture";
  id: string;
  size: readonly [number, number];
  format: TextureFormat;
  /** Who supplies frames. The runtime uploads; the plan ⊥ carry pixels (V63 clone-safe). */
  sourceId: string;
}
```
`sourceId` ⊥ the pixels: the plan stays structured-clone-safe (V63) ∴ worker-movable. the
runtime holds a registry `sourceId → MediaSource` and uploads on frame-ready.

### media as NODES (TD Movie File In / Movie File Out TOP)
recording belongs ∈ the GRAPH, ⊥ a global "record" button. TD makes it a node ∴ TOPOLOGY
decides what is recorded: an intermediate branch, several outputs at once, a pass you are
debugging — ⊥ only whatever the single main output happens to be.

- **MovieFileIn** — ONE node for STILL, SEQUENCE and VIDEO, as TD's Movie File In TOP is.
  ⊥ a separate ImageIn: the param set overlaps almost entirely (file, color space, alpha,
  filter/wrap, native res) and 2 nodes would mean choosing the wrong one before you know
  what the file is. a still simply has no timeline — playback params HIDE when the loaded
  asset has 1 frame, ⊥ sit there inert (V90: ⊥ show a control that does nothing).
  **NOTHING loads a file today** — the catalogue is entirely procedural, so this is the
  first node that reads from disk and the first real consumer of `AssetReference`.
  image | video | sequence → texture. play/pause/seek/loop/rate, in|out
  points, native res, current time, duration, frame-ready event. asset by `AssetReference`,
  ⊥ a raw path (V10). decode behind a media-source abstraction: `HTMLVideoElement` first,
  WebCodecs later where it measurably wins.
- **DeviceIn** (TD Video Device In TOP) — webcam | capture device → texture. SEPARATE node
  from MovieFileIn, as TD keeps them: the param sets barely overlap (device pick, resolution
  negotiation vs file + playback), and V122's hide-what-⊥-apply would hide most of either.
  rides the SAME `externalTexture` + media-source registry (T229) — a webcam is another
  `MediaSource`, ⊥ a subsystem. `getDisplayMedia` screen capture = the same shape, later.
  what a FILE never has to handle, and ∀ of it is normal ⊥ exceptional:
  permission denied · no device · device unplugged mid-stream · another app takes the camera ·
  tab backgrounded · resolution ⊥ what you asked for.
- **MovieFileOut** — a texture input → an encoded file. rides T111's WebCodecs mp4 +
  exact-frame capture. IS A SINK (V25) ∴ ⊥ pruned; recording is its side effect.

both are Phase 2 (media pipeline, doc §33) — but the SHAPE is decided now, because
"recording is a node" changes who owns the export interface, and retrofitting a global
recorder into a node model is a rewrite.

### node catalog guideline
TD TOP family = reference vocabulary for core node set — naming, param names, default behavior.
map where it maps, ⊥ clone. POP/SOP families → later phase, same approach.
per-node parity notes ∈ node manifest `description`, ⊥ ∈ spec.

### decided (was open, confirmed 2026-08-29)
- baseline: Chrome/Edge ≥ 128 desktop. min capability Tier B (rgba16float + compute + storage buffers). timestamp query optional. mobile excluded v1.
- headless: seam + CI parity test. ⊥ render queue v1.
- agent authority: graph edit | shader edit | param set = free + undoable, ⊥ confirm. local file | network | upload | export | recording | component install | project delete = capability grant + confirm.
- save: single `.loom.json` + external `AssetReference`. unresolved → relink flow. bundle → Phase 2.

### locked — owner interview 2026-08-29
- color: `space` ∈ `texture2d` port type. linear working space, decode @ load, encode+tonemap @ output only.
- param modulation: resolver invariant AND `ParameterValue` envelope `{kind:"static",value}` | reserved bound — both land now, before ∀ `.loom.json` ∈ wild. envelope passthrough lane fixes closed-union anti-V10.
- perform mode: full multi-window output = COMMITTED Phase 2 deliverable (multi display, VJ). presentation seam designed now, ⊥ prep-only.
- revision contention: param-only carve-out. value-only edits on disjoint entities ⊥ conflict w/ structural patch. amends V33.
- workers: renderer-in-worker COMMITTED Phase 2. worker owns device + ∀ surfaces; window transfers `OffscreenCanvas` in = also multi-window transport. v1 main-thread + clone-safe invariant + DOM-free lint + non-rAF loop.
- audio-reactive: early Phase 2 headline. AudioIn (mic|file) → analysis (FFT bands, beat, envelope) → params via resolver. first consumer proving modulation arch. WebMIDI alongside. OSC → Phase 3 (needs bridge).
- expressions: own minimal grammar. jsep-style AST, whitelisted fns, vars only ← `FrameEvaluationInput` + node ctx. deterministic + sandboxed by construction. v1 = arithmetic only, 1 evaluator module.
- autosave: IndexedDB ring. 2s debounce after last mutation. keep last 20 + 1 per 10min pinned, pins capped 48 (~8h; ⊥ multi-day session fills quota). restore-on-launch prompt. manual save still writes `.loom.json`. `serialize.ts` = sole serializer, shared w/ manual save.
- recording: first realtime export = WebCodecs → mp4 (`VideoEncoder`, exact-frame capture ← render loop). ⊥ MediaRecorder stopgap. Chrome ≥128 guarantees WebCodecs.

## §I INTERFACES

### file: `*.loom.json`
```ts
interface ProjectDocument {
  schemaVersion: number; projectId: string; name: string;
  graph: GraphDocument; settings: ProjectSettings;
  assets: AssetReference[]; createdAt: string; updatedAt: string;
}
interface GraphDocument {
  revision: number;
  nodes: Record<NodeId, GraphNode>; edges: Record<EdgeId, GraphEdge>;
  groups: Record<string, GraphGroup>; viewport?: ViewportState;
}
```
IDs opaque, globally unique strings. ⊥ array index as identity. `revision` monotonic, bumped per applied command.

### module: `src/runtime/backend` — sole vgpu boundary
```ts
interface RenderBackend {
  initialize(options: BackendInitOptions): Promise<BackendCapabilities>;
  compile(plan: LogicalExecutionPlan): Promise<CompiledExecutionPlan>;
  render(plan: CompiledExecutionPlan, frame: FrameInputs): void;
  resize(outputId: string, size: readonly [number, number]): void;
  readOutput(outputId: string): Promise<Uint8Array>;
  onDiagnostic(listener: (diagnostic: RuntimeDiagnostic) => void): () => void;
  dispose(): void;
}
```

### module: `src/domain/commands` — sole mutation path
```ts
interface AppCommandBus {
  query<TName extends QueryName>(
    name: TName, input: QueryInput<TName>, context: InvocationContext,
  ): Promise<QueryOutput<TName>>;
  execute<TName extends CommandName>(
    name: TName, input: CommandInput<TName>, context: InvocationContext,
  ): Promise<CommandResult<TName>>;
}
interface InvocationContext {
  actor: { kind: "human" | "agent" | "system"; id: string; label?: string };
  projectId: string;
  capabilities: CapabilityGrant[];
  transactionId?: string;
  dryRun?: boolean;
}
```
callers: toolbar, menu, keybind, inspector edit, drag-connect, tests, agent adapters.

### type: atomic graph patch
```ts
interface GraphPatch {
  baseRevision: number;
  operations: GraphPatchOperation[];
  label?: string;
}
interface GraphPatchResult {
  status: "applied" | "rejected" | "conflict";
  revision: number;
  appliedOperations: number;
  diagnostics: RuntimeDiagnostic[];
  createdIds: Record<string, string>;
  undoGroupId?: string;
}
```
patch-local temp IDs → stable IDs via `createdIds`. lets agent add N nodes + wire them in 1 request.

### type: port union
```ts
type PortType =
  | { kind: "texture2d"; sample: "float" | "unfilterable-float" | "depth"; channels?: 1 | 2 | 4 }
  | { kind: "buffer"; element: string; access: "read" | "write" | "read-write" }
  | { kind: "scalar"; scalar: "f32" | "i32" | "u32" | "bool" }
  | { kind: "vector"; scalar: "f32" | "i32" | "u32"; size: 2 | 3 | 4 }

### type: pointset port (replaces unimplemented `geometry`)
```ts
interface PointAttributeSpec {
  name: string;                       // "P", "vel", "age", "Cd" — arbitrary, day 1
  type: "f32" | "vec2f" | "vec3f" | "vec4f" | "i32" | "u32" | "mat3x3f" | "mat4x4f";
}
type PortType =
  | …
  | { kind: "pointset"; requires: PointAttributeSpec[]; topology?: "points" | "lines" | "triangles" };
```
compat (V13 spirit): consumer's `requires` ! be satisfied by producer's attributes — name AND
type exact. superset OK (producer may carry more), missing|mistyped = ⊥. topology absent = particles.

### kernel ABI
```wgsl
fn process(p: Point, ctx: KernelContext) -> Point
```
`Point` struct codegen'd from attribute schema. `ctx` carries frame input + `pointId`.
`NodeDefinition.contractVersion` pins ABI; mismatch → diagnostic, ⊥ silent run.

### type: component (COMP) — subgraph behind a stable interface
```ts
interface GraphComponentDefinition {
  componentId: ComponentId;
  version: number;
  name: string;
  graph: GraphDocument;              // internal network
  inputs: ExposedPort[];             // internal port → external port
  outputs: ExposedPort[];
  parameters: PublishedParameter[];  // internal params → component param page
  migrations?: ComponentMigration[];
  description?: string;
  capabilities?: CapabilityRequirement[];  // what the internal network needs (V38)
}

interface ExposedPort { externalId: PortId; label: string; nodeId: NodeId; portId: PortId; }

/** One component param drives N internal targets — TD binds a custom par to many. */
interface PublishedParameter {
  key: string;                       // name on the component's param page
  definition: ParameterDefinition;   // label, range, unit, default — re-authored, ⊥ copied
  targets: ReadonlyArray<{ nodeId: NodeId; key: string }>;
}
```
instance stores `componentId` + `version` + own param values + overrides.
⊥ duplicate internal graph unless detached.

### parent scope
child reads owning component's params via resolver (V61): `parent.<key>`.
resolves ∀ nesting depth by walking up instance chain. ⊥ arbitrary cross-node reads —
`parent` = lexical, ⊥ a graph edge.

### type: context menu (right-click) — data, ⊥ hardcoded
```ts
interface MenuTarget {
  surface: "canvas" | "node" | "port" | "edge" | "parameter";
  nodeId?: NodeId; portId?: PortId; edgeId?: EdgeId; parameterKey?: string;
}
interface MenuItem {
  command: CommandName;   // ⊥ inline handler — same path as hotkey + palette (V29, V52)
  input?: unknown;
  label: string;
  when?: string;
  submenu?: MenuItem[];
}
```
ONE menu root per surface, target resolved from event on open. ⊥ Radix root per node —
dense graph cost. keys rendered ← keymap (V55), ⊥ literal "⌘Z" strings.

### parameter modes — TD parity (verified vs docs.derivative.ca)
TD: ∀ parameter has a MODE. click the param NAME to expand → 4 square mode buttons.
grey=Constant · blue=Expression · green=Export(CHOP-driven) · purple=Bind(bi-directional).
right-click = popup menu. ctrl/cmd+E = edit the expression.

**THE DETAIL THAT MATTERS**: an inactive mode that HAS a value shows a small square ∈ the
button's lower-left corner. ∴ **each mode retains its own value independently** — switching
to Constant ⊥ destroys the expression. that is why the indicator exists, and it is what
makes mode-switching safe to experiment with.

```ts
type ParameterBinding =
  | { kind: "static"; value: ParameterValue }
  | { kind: "expression"; source: string }            // OUR grammar (V71), ⊥ Python
  | { kind: "bind"; ref: string }                     // another param | `parent.<key>`
  | { kind: "driven"; channel: string };              // TD Export analog — audio|MIDI|LFO, Phase 2

interface ParameterSlot {
  mode: ParameterBinding["kind"];
  /** EVERY mode's last value, kept. mode switch ⊥ destructive. */
  bindings: Partial<Record<ParameterBinding["kind"], ParameterBinding>>;
}
```
∀ parameter TYPE takes ∀ mode — number, vector, color, bool, enum, string alike. ⊥ a
number-only feature: TD drives menus + toggles from expressions & that is half its power.

### Composite node + individual blend nodes — BOTH, sharing one implementation
TD ships a Composite TOP w/ an Operation menu AND standalone Add/Multiply/etc. keep both:
- **Composite** — variadic inputs + an `operation` ENUM. flexible: change the blend w/o
  rewiring, drive the mode by expression (V107), reach a mode you ⊥ have a node for.
- **Over/Add/Multiply/Screen/Difference** — fixed operation. a graph reading `Multiply`
  says what it does at a glance; `Composite` makes you open it. when you KNOW the op, the
  named node is the better documentation.

**⊥ two implementations of the blend math.** blend fns live ∈ 1 WGSL module; Composite
selects @ compile time; a named node binds a fixed selection of the SAME fn. else Over ∈
Composite and the Over node drift & only one gets the bug fix.

`operation` is `compileTime: true` — it changes the SHADER, ⊥ a uniform. specialise per
mode (the shader cache already keys on constants) ⊥ branch per pixel: a per-pixel switch
on a value that changes ~never is the wrong trade, and V5's uniform-only fast path stays
meaningful only if mode changes are honestly classified as structural.

### variadic inputs (1+n) — the mechanism exists, ⊥ node uses it
`PortDefinition.variadic` is ∈ the contract, honored by the patch layer (V14), the
compiler (`CompiledInputBinding` is an ARRAY per port), and the canvas. **⊥ production
node declares one** — only test fixtures. same shape as feedback before T152: every layer
built, nothing reaching it.

Composite (Over/Add/Multiply/Screen/Difference) is the obvious first consumer — TD's
Composite TOP is multi-input. Also: Switch, Merge, and any "combine N of these" op.

**THE GAP THAT MATTERS**: edges into one port currently arrive in EDGE-ID order — i.e.
creation order — and `GraphEdge` carries no ordering field. For Over, **layer order IS the
operation**. Wiring a third layer would land it wherever its id sorted, and reordering
would mean deleting and rewiring. ∴ a variadic port needs an EXPLICIT order before any node
can use one.

### node NAMES are identifiers, ⊥ decoration (TD: noise1, noise2, null1)
prerequisite for expressions & binds: `op('noise1').par.period` only works because a name
is UNIQUE within its network. ∴ names must land BEFORE reference syntax, ⊥ after.

- ∀ node has a `name`, unique within its graph. auto-numbered on collision: `noise1`,
  `noise2` — created from the definition type, lowercased.
- rename to a taken name → auto-suffix, ⊥ reject. the user's intent is the WORD; the
  number is bookkeeping.
- `name` (identifier, unique, referenceable) ≠ a comment (free text, ⊥ unique). today's
  `GraphNode.label` conflates them — it is display-only & unconstrained. `label` BECOMES
  the name; a separate comment field arrives when someone wants one.
- rename ! rewrite references that named it, or the rename silently breaks a bind (V110).
  ∴ rename is a graph-wide patch, ⊥ a node-local one.

**Null node** — TD `null1` idiom: 1 in, 1 out, passes through untouched. exists to be a
STABLE REFERENCE POINT: reference `null1` & rewire upstream freely w/o touching any
reference. cheap (⊥ pass emitted — compiler passes the binding through), and the standard
place to park a bookmark ∈ a big graph.

### pulse parameters (TD Pulse) — momentary triggers
TD: `Pulse` is a parameter TYPE, ⊥ a per-node feature. Feedback TOP has Reset; Timer has
Start/Stop. ∴ ANY node can declare one and the mechanism is written once.

```ts
interface PulseParameter extends ParameterBase { type: "pulse"; }
```
- momentary: it FIRES, it ⊥ hold. never serialized as "on" — a pulse ∈ a saved doc that
  re-fires on load would reset your work every time you opened it.
- mutates RUNTIME state, ⊥ document state ∴ audited (V31) but **⊥ undoable**: undo restores
  a document, and a cleared feedback buffer is ⊥ ∈ the document. saying so beats a
  disabled undo that silently does nothing.
- takes ∀ mode (V107) — an EXPRESSION firing a pulse is how an automated reset happens
  (TD's whole idiom: pulse on a beat, on a threshold, on a frame count).
- TD also pairs a HOLD toggle w/ the momentary pulse (Feedback TOP has both). support both:
  `reset` (hold ∈ reset) + `resetPulse` (fire once).

a node declaring `stateful.reset === true` (V46, already ∈ the contract) SHOULD expose one
— that field has been declaring the capability w/ nothing to trigger it.
consumers: Feedback (clear), Noise (reseed), accumulator (clear), point sim (reset),
MovieFileIn (re-fetch).

### compound parameters are COMPONENT-ADDRESSABLE (TD: colorr/colorg/colorb, tx/ty/tz)
TD has ⊥ "a color parameter" — it has `colorr`, `colorg`, `colorb`, each a first-class
parameter w/ its OWN mode. the swatch is a convenience ON TOP. same for `tx`/`ty`/`tz`.
that is what makes a single channel drivable while the others stay constant.

ours: the MANIFEST keeps one declaration (`color`, `t`) — verbose 4-way manifests would
be worse — but the SLOT is per component:
```
color  → color.r  color.g  color.b  color.a
t      → t.x      t.y      t.z      (t.w for size 4)
```
∀ component gets its own `ParameterSlot` ∴ its own mode, expression, bind, value.
resolver reassembles components → the compound value the shader wants.
component names: r g b a · x y z w.

### type: per-node output resolution override (TD Common page)
```ts
type NodeResolutionOverride =
  | { mode: "auto" }                                   // node's own ResolutionPolicy — DEFAULT
  | { mode: "project" }                                // project output resolution
  | { mode: "input"; input?: PortId }                  // inherit named input
  | { mode: "scale"; factor: number; input?: PortId }  // 1/8 1/4 1/2 2x 4x 8x
  | { mode: "fixed"; width: number; height: number };  // custom
```
lives on `GraphNode.resolution?`. absent → definition policy. instance state, ⊥ definition state.

TD Output Resolution menu = Use Input | Eighth | Quarter | Half | 2X | 4X | 8X |
Fit Resolution | Limit Resolution | Custom. our `scale` covers eighth..8x, `fixed` = custom.
MISSING: `fit` (fit w/h, keep aspect) + `limit` (clamp w/h). both real, both useful —
`limit` = safety valve. → wave 2 barrier (union growth, tracks E+G reading it now).

### type: per-node pixel format override (TD Common page)
```ts
type NodeFormatOverride =
  | { mode: "auto" }                          // node's own FormatPolicy — DEFAULT
  | { mode: "project" }                       // project workingFormat
  | { mode: "input"; input?: PortId }         // Use Input
  | { mode: "fixed"; format: TextureFormat }; // rgba8unorm | rgba16float | r32float
```
lives on `GraphNode.format?`. depth ⊥ selectable — color outputs only.
`rgba8unorm-srgb` landed @ barrier. `TEXTURE_FORMATS` const = single source, type derived from it.

### module: `src/editor/keymap` — bindings as data
```ts
type KeyContext = "global" | "graph" | "inspector" | "viewer" | "text";

interface KeyBinding {
  id: string;              // stable, survives rebinding
  keys: string;            // "mod+z", "shift+h", "g d" (chord)
  context: KeyContext;     // narrowest wins; "text" swallows editing keys
  command: CommandName;    // bus command — ⊥ inline handler
  input?: unknown;         // static args, or resolved from selection
  when?: string;           // guard: "hasSelection", "nodeHovered"
  label: string;           // shown in palette, menus, tooltips
}

interface Keymap {
  defaults: KeyBinding[];
  overrides: Record<string, string | null>;  // id → keys, null = unbound
}
```
`mod` = Cmd @ macOS, Ctrl elsewhere. overrides ∈ localStorage, ⊥ ∈ project doc.

  total_cooks                      →  framesRendered

### custom WGSL node contract v1
```wgsl
@group(0) @binding(0) var inputSampler: sampler;
@group(0) @binding(1) var inputTexture: texture_2d<f32>;

// Shared frame block — the runtime fills it from FrameEvaluationInput every frame.
// TIME LIVES HERE AND NOWHERE ELSE (V44).
@group(0) @binding(3) var<uniform> frameU: SharedFrame;

struct Params { amount: f32 };
@group(0) @binding(2) var<uniform> params: Params;

@fragment
fn fs(@location(0) uv: vec2f) -> @location(0) vec4f {
  return textureSample(inputTexture, inputSampler, uv);
}
```
`Params` ⊥ carries `time`. per-pass uniform block written @ compile + on param change
(V5, V21) ∴ structurally ⊥ carry a per-frame clock — a `time` field there = a value that
silently never advances. `frameU.time` = its only home.

binding is GATED, ⊥ unconditional: runtime binds by NAME and hard-errors on a name the
shader ⊥ declare (`VGPU-RING1-UNSUPPORTED`). `compile()` scans the source and binds only
what it asked for — a kernel declaring neither block (E2 Gray-Scott) ! still compile.

## §V INVARIANTS

V1: domain graph = truth. React Flow node array ⊥ execution source.
V2: React component ⊥ encode GPU command. WebGPU calls only ∈ `src/runtime/`.
V3: `vgpu` import only ∈ `src/runtime/backend/vgpu/`. lint-enforced.
V4: current-frame graph = DAG. cycle legal ⟺ ∀ path in cycle crosses explicit temporal node.
V5: uniform-value param change → update uniform only. ⊥ recompile.
V6: output w/ N consumers → rendered 1× per frame, texture reused ∀ N.
V7: preview GPU→GPU. readback ⊥ in playback loop — export/inspect/test only.
V8: ⊥ render-target alloc inside frame loop. effects/targets/samplers/buffers created outside.
V9: shader compile fail → last valid plan retained + output flagged stale. ⊥ blank frame.
V10: ∀ serialized doc has `schemaVersion` + per-node `definitionVersion`. unknown node preserved as placeholder, ⊥ dropped.
V11: ∀ node definition runs headless. ⊥ import React or @xyflow.
V12: optional GPU feature discovered via capability report before use. ⊥ assumed.
V13: connect requires exact `PortType` match. ⊥ implicit color-space/format/scalar/resolution conversion. conversion = visible node.
V14: input port accepts ≤ 1 incoming edge unless declared variadic. output fan-out unbounded.
V14b: an EDGE is a valid drop target for a connection. release over the line → the drag takes that edge's TARGET and replaces it. the line is a big target; the port is a 7px dot (V99) — requiring the dot when the wire is right there is asking for precision the task ⊥ need.
V14c: edge hit area ! be generous (~10px each side of the stroke, invisible), same principle as V99. a 1px stroke is ⊥ a target. NOTE the ~10px is a CURSOR tolerance ∈ SCREEN space. a NODE dropped on an edge (V14d) needs a different unit — a band through the node's middle, ¼ height either side, ∈ GRAPH space — & someone will otherwise "correct" it to 10px.
V14d: dropping a NODE on an edge splices it, & the hit test runs ∈ GRAPH space (both the node box & the wire are graph-space facts, unlike a cursor) ∴ identical @ any zoom. a BAND, ⊥ the whole rectangle: rect-vs-curve silently rewires a graph whenever a node is parked near a wire passing behind it, which is far worse than a gesture needing a 2nd try. REFUSE when the node is already an end of the edge, when ⊥ port pair fits (V13), or when the splice would close a loop (V4).
V14e: the drag-onto-edge gesture is SYMMETRIC — a drag begun @ an INPUT takes the edge's SOURCE, mirroring V14b's target case. both ends are draggable & a 1-way gesture reads as a bug.
V14a: dropping a connection on an OCCUPIED input REPLACES the existing edge — 1 patch, 1 undo group (V32, V34). ⊥ silently refuse: the user's intent is unambiguous and refusing makes them hunt for the old edge to delete first.
V15: ∀ semantic edit undoable. continuous drag coalesced → 1 history entry, live values still applied.
V16: per-frame metrics & preview pixels ⊥ enter document store. UI metric refresh ≤ 10 Hz.
V17: theme dark-only v1. ∀ color from CSS var token. ⊥ hardcoded hex in component. a color FUNCTION deriving from a token (`color-mix(in srgb, var(--x) 30%, transparent)`) = allowed — it introduces no literal & is the only way to express a translucent tint of a themed color. a literal ANYWHERE inside one, incl. nested, = caught.
V18: pane sizes persisted ∈ localStorage, ⊥ ∈ project doc.
V19: ∀ interactive control keyboard reachable, visible focus ring, `prefers-reduced-motion` honored (edge flow anim → static).
V20: param control drag ⊥ start graph pan | node drag | selection.
V21: resolution & format propagation deterministic, happens @ compile/resize. ⊥ per-frame.
V22: feedback = stable ping-pong pair. swap after ∀ current-frame consumers encoded.
V23: device lost → halt submit, report diagnostic, rebuild resources from domain graph, reset temporal history.
V24: caps enforced before dispatch — resolution, dispatch size, buffer bytes, point count, attribute count, per-point stride. ∀ checked vs `capabilities.limits` + `settings.limits`. project memory budget reported. over-cap → diagnostic + refuse, ⊥ device loss.
V25: compiler evaluates only nodes reachable backward from active sinks. rest pruned.
V26: edge visual hue = source port family color (§C). ⊥ arbitrary edge color.
V27: WGSL compile message maps to editor line+col, surfaces on node badge + problems tab.
V28: only visible|pinned previews scheduled. offscreen/collapsed node preview suspended.
V28b: a VISIBLE texture-producing node previews BY DEFAULT — TD parity: a disconnected node shows its output, ⊥ a blank box. ∴ visibility (⊥ `ui.preview`) is what makes it a preview sink. `ui.preview` = an explicit PIN — keep previewing while scrolled off — ⊥ the on-switch. w/o this a node renders nothing until wired to an Output, which reads as broken & hides the node you are authoring.
V28c: default-on previews are affordable ONLY because V28 suspends offscreen|collapsed. a 200-node graph previews the ~dozen on screen. ∴ V28b ⊥ shippable w/o V28's scheduler — they land together.
V28a: explicit sink list = AUTHORITATIVE ∀ previews — empty list means NONE visible, ⊥ "fall back to the flags". `undefined` = use document `ui.preview` flags. ∴ composition root ! pass ∀ visible previews once it derives them, ⊥ rely on the union.
V29: ∀ mutation → `AppCommandBus.execute`. ⊥ adapter mutates zustand | React Flow array | GPU resource directly.
V30: ∀ command carries `InvocationContext.actor`. ⊥ anonymous mutation.
V31: ∀ mutation → `AuditEntry`. recent window inspectable ∈ UI; ring bound 512 — ⊥ a bug: an unbounded log grows quadratically over a 60Hz drag session. durable full audit → IndexedDB append task if ever needed.
V32: `GraphPatch` atomic — ∀ ops apply | 0 apply.
V33: stale `baseRevision` → `conflict` ⟺ actual entity overlap. ⊥ silent rebase. patch ops classified value-only (param, position, ui) | structural (add, remove, connect, disconnect). value-only on disjoint entities ⊥ conflict w/ concurrent structural patch — else 60Hz human drag starves ∀ agent patch (T62 gate passes quiet, unusable next to live human).
V34: 1 patch → 1 undo group unless explicitly split.
V35: patch temp IDs resolved to stable IDs, returned ∈ `createdIds`.
V36: `dryRun: true` → validate + return diagnostics, ⊥ mutate, ⊥ audit as applied.
V37: tool result = structured data, ⊥ instruction to calling model. 3rd-party node text & project text = untrusted.
V38: capability grant required per class: local file, network, upload, export, recording, component install, project delete. calling tool ⊥ grants permission. ⟶ ⚠**COUNT CORRECTED — THE CODE HAS *NINE*, ⊥ SEVEN: `viewportControl` was an unlisted EIGHTH & §T1220 added `previewSnapshot` as the NINTH.** & the ninth is the one that shows the class list is a DESIGN SURFACE rather than a tally: **`previewSnapshot` EXISTS ∵ *EXPORT* & *A THUMBNAIL THE USER IS ALREADY LOOKING AT* ARE DIFFERENT ACTS W/ DIFFERENT RISK, & GATING THEM AS ONE MADE THE GATE THE WRONG SHAPE RATHER THAN TOO STRICT.** ∴ when a refusal feels wrong, ask whether the CLASS is wrong before asking whether the POLICY is|
V39: bus adapter-agnostic. WebMCP | MCP server adapter = transport + schema only, 0 app-logic duplication.
V40: node delete → incident edges removed|tombstoned deterministically, same result ∀ actors. binds undo/redo RESTORE too, ⊥ only `removeNodes` op — restore ! refuse rather than leave a dangling edge (V65).
V41: undo actor-local. ⊥ erase other actor work. FULLY-blocked undo|redo → `rejected` + entry RETAINED, ⊥ revision bump, ⊥ "applied" audit for a no-op. blocked ← owner conflict OR referential integrity (V65) alike. partially-blocked → apply rest, consume, push to redo.
V42: agent activity visible — planning | editing | compiling | awaiting-approval shown in UI. ⊥ invisible background mutation.
V43: long render | sim cancellable.
V44: ∀ time-dependent node consumes `FrameEvaluationInput`. ⊥ read `Date.now` | `performance.now` | rAF directly. lint-enforced.

V46: stateful node declares `{reset, deterministicReplay, checkpoint, randomAccess}` ∈ manifest.

V48: ∀ readback isolated behind export interface. ⊥ readback call outside it.
V49: runtime ⊥ couple graph eval to rAF | wall clock. scheduler = swappable transport source.
V51: node format override = instance state, @ compile, ⊥ per-frame. absent → definition `formatPolicy`. ! validated vs capability report (V12) — unsupported → diagnostic + documented fallback, ⊥ crash, ⊥ silent swap. depth format ⊥ on color output. change → recreate targets + reset feedback (V22).
V56: project working space = linear RGB. import|media node decodes → linear. encode + tonemap ONLY @ output|display node. texture carrying non-color data flagged `data`, bypasses ∀ conversion. ⊥ node silently mixes encoded & linear.
V57: `texture2d` carries `space: "linear"|"encoded"|"data"`. exact-match under V13 — absent = linear (`colorSpaceOf`). ∈ propagation absent = NO CLAIM, derived fills it (`declaredColorSpace`). mismatch → diagnostic naming conversion node to insert, ⊥ silent convert.

V57c: ⚑**AMENDMENT, ORCHESTRATOR RULED (§T768): a `texture2d` INPUT declared `space:"data"` ACCEPTS ANY SOURCE SPACE — reading bytes AS DATA IS ⊥ A CONVERSION.** §V13's refusal is about IMPLICIT CONVERSION & **a data input CONVERTS NOTHING**. ⚑**THE DECIDING FACT: THE COMPILER ALREADY BELIEVES THIS** — `compile.ts`'s space propagation has carried EXACTLY this rule since §T83/§B5, its comment citing §V57 (*a Mask's mask input takes any channel as coverage, & that is ⊥ a colour mismatch*) ∴ **today only the CONNECT gate (`arePortsCompatible`) DISAGREES W/ THE COMPILER'S OWN PROPAGATION**: the 2 halves of §V57 are ALREADY SPLIT, & this amendment **REUNIFIES them ON THE COMPILER'S SIDE** rather than loosening anything. **THE REFUSAL THAT STAYS — & IS THE ACTUAL PROTECTION — IS THE ASYMMETRIC ONE: a `data` OUTPUT into a COLOUR input still REFUSES**, ∵ a consumer would DISPLAY-DECODE a depth map (§T722's retreat, correctly refused). ⚠**§V57a does ⊥ ride along**: `displace.disp` deliberately FILTERS its field (low-res noise driving smooth full-res displacement is the canonical use) & §V57b already keeps that legal — **`space` ⊥ silently changes sampling**|V13,V57,V57a,V57b,T83,B5,T768,T722

### cooking — TD's model, Notch's stateless/stateful split (T249-T256)
TD: cook needs BOTH a REQUEST (downstream | param reference | viewer) & a REASON (input
cooked | param changed | time-dependent | expression resolves ≠). PULL, ⊥ push. cook graph =
wires ∪ PARAMETER REFERENCES. escape hatches @ both ends (Cook Type, Cooking Flag).
Notch: push-traverse active tree from Root ∀ frame, ⊥ dirty mechanism, per-node manual
"static" switches. worse — but 3 ideas better than TD's:
 1. STATELESS vs STATEFUL as a per-node property (the thing TD lacks & we need most)
 2. a frozen node ! COMPUTE ONCE before it may serve cache; clears on reset
 3. CPU+GPU ms together per node, category rollups
TD's own failure worth ⊥ inheriting: dependency system ⊥ total; when it misses it shows a
STALE value as FRESH. documented (`Dependency.modified()` exists for this) & unroot-caused
∈ the field. ∴ our gate is built BEFORE the feature, ⊥ after.

LAYERING — 3 rows, ⊥ 1: compile = does node EXIST. build = which GPU objects REUSED
(carry-over, already built). cook = does this pass RUN THIS FRAME. cooking is only row 3.
unit = NODE ⊥ pass (Blur's 2 passes share a node-private scratch).

V174: ∈ the inspector, PARAMETERS come first & COMMON is a separate TAB (TD's page model) — ⊥ both stacked on 1 page. common is chrome you set once; parameters are the work. prime real estate goes to the work.
V175: a Ramp is N STOPS, ⊥ 2 colours. add|remove|move a stop, position per stop. 2-colour is the degenerate case of the general thing, & shipping only the degenerate case means every gradient anyone actually wants is impossible.
### jitter ∈ `time * k` — ⊥ rounding, it's the CLOCK (B21)
`liveClock` accumulates WALL deltas (clamped, epoch 0 — both already right). but rAF deltas
jitter ~16.6ms ± several ∴ `time` advances NON-UNIFORMLY ∴ `time * 0.15` on a translate
steps unevenly. spatially straight, temporally ragged. ⊥ f32, ⊥ JS rounding — f64 on CPU,
& they already start @ 0 which is the real f32 mitigation.
TD's answer: 2 clocks. `absTime.seconds` = wall. timeline time = frame/fps, UNIFORM BY
CONSTRUCTION. animation uses the timeline one.
TRADE, stated: timeline time means dropped frames SLOW the animation (TD behaves this way);
wall time means dropped frames SKIP it (Notch's "frame-rate independence" = "visually
similar", ⊥ identical). ⊥ 1 right answer ∴ ship both & DEFAULT to smooth.

### the VALUE GRAPH — TD's CHOP network, ⊥ a 2nd product (T273-T277)

∈ a parameter string is ⊥ a graph, it's a graph typed as text.
TD wires CHOPs w/ cables ∴ so do we. a `value` PORT TYPE, value EDGES, & a CPU-side graph
evaluated ∀ frame BEFORE the render. this is the same split TD has (CHOP network vs TOP
network) ∈ 1 canvas.

V202: the frame loop follows the VISIBLE surface. when a perform window is open, IT hosts the scheduler. Chrome clamps rAF to ~1Hz ∈ a non-foreground tab & suspends it entirely after a while ∴ an editor tab backgrounded while a perform window shows output means THE SHOW FREEZES. that is a real failure mode for a TD replacement, ⊥ a test artefact. background timers are throttled too ∴ the robust answers are the perform window's own context, or the worker + OffscreenCanvas already committed for Phase 2.
V203: when rAF cadence COLLAPSES while playing, SAY SO. compare wall time to frame count (cheap) & surface "throttled by the browser". a frozen picture w/ ⊥ explanation is indistinguishable from a bug — & it generated ~6 "nothing animates" reports before anyone worked out what it was.
V209: a heal-on-any-edit path is a LATCH waiting for the edit rate to drop. T258's dirty-preview retry runs @ `backend.compile`, & today EVERY edit lands there ∴ any knob turn heals a dirty preview. wire the classifier & only STRUCTURAL edits land there — a preview that went dirty ∈ a race stays black through any amount of knob-turning. ∴ a recovery path ! be driven by something that happens UNCONDITIONALLY (frame entry), ⊥ by a path an optimisation is about to make conditional. same species as B24's retry gated on a condition only true before the 1st compile.
V210: the compile gate has SEVERAL independent structural triggers & the document revision is only ONE. an input producing ⊥ document edit is INVISIBLE to a document-keyed gate. the enumeration, so it is ⊥ rediscovered 1 at a time:
 (a) SINK SET — opening|closing a preview. ⊥ document edit @ all ∴ nothing to classify. a revision-keyed gate stops materializing a sink the moment someone opens a preview.
 (b) BACKEND CAPABILITIES on device recovery — a plan compiled against tier-B needs recompiling if the recovered adapter differs. covered today: the recovery path rebuilds from the retained plan.
 (c) COMPONENT CATALOGUE edits (V82) — editing a component's INTERNAL graph changes what flattening produces WITHOUT touching the host document. live-ness depends on how component edits reach the store; ⊥ assumed either way, ! be checked.
 (d) `project.setSettings` (T272) — settings are COMPILE INPUT. presumably a document revision, but presumption is the failure mode this invariant exists for.
V218: prefer the EXACT claim; when a range assertion FAILS, ask whether the exact value is derivable before loosening it. T299 asserted "≥4 distinct lit intensities" on a sphere of axis-aligned boxes & got 3 — because two-sided lambert reads |x·L|, |y·L|, |z·L| & `abs` collapses the ± face pairs. the range was the WRONG assertion & the device said so. companion to V147: a range assertion TOLERATES the bug, & a failing one is often the geometry teaching the stronger claim.
V219: a per-shape `vertexCount` would make SHAPE structural. all shapes draw the same 36 verts & shorter ones collapse their tail into ZERO-AREA triangles ∴ switching shape is 1 integer upload & V5 holds. the naive version is correct & silently costs a recompile per shape change.
### vgpu UPSTREAM GAPS — report these, ⊥ re-derive them
1. **⊥ uncaptured-error forwarding.** `onError` carries vgpu's OWN scoped errors ONLY; the device's `onuncapturederror` path is never forwarded ∴ a bind-group | dispatch-time verdict had ⊥ route to ANYTHING, even during a compile window. B9's listener was never the whole hole & B33 was the proof. we now attach 2 nets (vgpu onError + the raw device's handler through the §V3-sanctioned reach-through).
2. ⊥ frame-level COMPUTE PASS hook — `compute.dispatch()` submits immediately (B19/V168).
3. ⊥ compute `timestampWrites` (T181) — compute passes are unmeasurable.

V262: **FALSE ALARMS teach people to ignore REAL ones ∴ V243 is ⊥ symmetric across a compound.** a component w/ its OWN stored slot resolves on its own terms — forwarding the compound's diagnostic would flag a GOOD channel. a component w/ ⊥ slot INHERITS the compound's number, so it ! inherit its diagnostic too. propagate a diagnostic exactly where the VALUE is inherited, ⊥ everywhere it could be.
V263: a GATE's granularity ! match the READER's granularity. `op('b').par.y` resolves b's WHOLE schema ∴ `a.x → b.y` + `b.z → a.w` genuinely recurses though the 2 parameter chains never touch — node-granular is CORRECT, ⊥ conservative. a finer gate would ACCEPT documents the reader then refuses 1 hop down, which is V243's invisible failure. if the reader ever resolves a single parameter ∈ isolation, both halves move together (pinned).
V264: a gate that blocks REPAIR is worse than the thing it gates. the patch gate is scoped to the EDITED node, ⊥ the document: a file can arrive holding a cycle, & refusing every unrelated edit until it is fixed makes the file harder to repair than to abandon. editing a node INSIDE the loop is still refused.
V259: **`auto` is ⊥ frame-identical to `always` TODAY, & the cause is ORDERING ⊥ the gate.** measured over 8 frames of a static plan whose brightness starts moving @ frame 3: `always` encodes 15,1,1,1,1,1,1,1; `auto` encodes 15,0,0,**0**,1,1,1,1 — frame 3 is SKIPPED & its value appears @ frame 4. that is EXACTLY the 1-frame lag V157 names as the signature failure, & V157's whole point is that it self-corrects ∴ an end-state comparison would pass. the uniform push runs ∈ the frame callback AFTER `render` has asked the gate ∴ the dirty mark arrives too late for the encode it belongs to. `always` stays the default; the switch is reachable & someone ! choose it, which is what V157 describes.
V260: when a FIXTURE lacks a contract method, give the FIXTURE the method — ⊥ make the caller defensive. 8 backend fixtures implemented every method but `setCookPolicy`, & an optional call would have let the app tolerate a backend that ⊥ implement its contract, which is how a missing wire HIDES. a fixture is construction-complete so ports wire; that is its job.
V261: to add a line to a file another track is EDITING: build the file as **HEAD + your line**, commit that path, then restore their working-tree version w/ your line preserved. HEAD gets your fix & none of their in-flight work; their worktree is untouched & their eventual commit ⊥ revert you. verified both ends.
V256: **a baseline DEFAULT is ⊥ a ceiling — ASK, clamped.** `maxStorageBuffersPerShaderStage = 8` is what a device gets when it asks for NOTHING, & we passed `requiredFeatures` & never `requiredLimits`. SAFE to raise because `describeCapabilities` reads `gpu.device.limits` — the NEGOTIATED value, ⊥ the adapter's — so the report & T328's validator follow automatically (`bindings.ts` reads `capabilities.limits[k]` w/ the baseline table as an ABSENT-KEY fallback, ⊥ a hardcoded floor). over-requesting FAILS device creation ∴ clamp per key. **⊥ headroom promises**: an earlier draft of THIS line said "desktop adapters offer 10-64+" & measurement says Dawn/Metal offers **10**. the win is real (8→10 is exactly what the 9-buffer failure needed); the framing was invented. V206 applies to invariants as much as to rows.

V625: **a SAW drives a WALKED angle; a ROTATION wants a SINE @ the same frequency.** a saw's wrap is CONTINUOUS once you take its cosine (an angle the herd walks) & DISCONTINUOUS as a rotation — it SNAPS BACK once a lap. ∴ same clock, same period, different reader ∴ ⊥ re-use the driver, re-shape it|T671,V481
V626: **to break a PATTERN, move the MEDIUM — ⊥ rotate the pattern.** a Gray-Scott lattice needs a STATIONARY substrate ∴ ADVECTION through a STATIC parameter field SHEARS it apart, while a RIGID ROTATION turns the lattice & leaves it a lattice. E32: `displace` between `state1` & the reaction, w/ `pack1` repainting b from `dish1` AFTER the reaction ∴ the field moves & its parameters do ⊥. ⚠ COST, measured: advection eats COVERAGE — @ weight 0.006 dark fraction → 71% & the pasture visibly SHRANK ∵ flow moves V faster than a low-feed regime regrows it ∴ 0.0025 chosen against that; the weight is the density knob|T671,V623,V554 ⟶ **CONFIRMED IN THE WILD & EXTENDED (T734).** ⚠**E24 ALREADY HAD A NODE ∈ THIS SLOT DOING THE WRONG THING**: `wind1`, a `transform` w/ `r: 0.02` between `state` & `rd` — **a RIGID ROTATION applied 17–24× PER FRAME**, precisely what this row says turns a lattice & leaves it a lattice. swapping it for ADVECTION (`displace` from a slow 2-channel perlin, `mono` OFF) **beats the rotation on motion @ EVERY age & multiplies live spot count 2–4×** (f1800: motion .0462 → **.0624**, spots 238 → **907**). **& the COST curve TURNS OVER**: on E2 (substeps 20 ∴ E32's .0025/frame is **.000125** here) dark rises MONOTONICALLY as recorded, **but MOTION PEAKS ~.00025 & FALLS above ~.0005** — past that **the flow REMOVES THE MATERIAL THAT WAS DOING THE MOVING** ∴ the weight has a measurable OPTIMUM, ⊥ only a ceiling
V627: **ADDITIVE point density is RESOLUTION-DEPENDENT ∴ a look call @ HALF RES LIES.** same point count into half the pixels = ~4× the per-texel accumulation ∴ a half-res render BLOWS OUT where the full-res one is correct (found shipping E35). ∴ ∀ look judgement on an additive-points document ! be made @ the project's FULL resolution, & a preview tile is ⊥ evidence about the OUTPUT's exposure. pairs w/ §V618: wrong ENCODING & wrong RESOLUTION are 2 separate ways a saved frame misreports a look|V618,T660,V471
V628: **PREVIEW tiles force `a = 1.0` ∴ they are STRUCTURALLY BLIND to source alpha ∴ ⊥ preview gate can ever verify the VIEWER's compositing.** every lens shader (`debug-effects.wgsl.ts`) writes alpha 1; the viewer BLITS SOURCE alpha (`BLIT_WGSL`) ∴ 6 preview gates stayed GREEN while the product presented BLACK. 7th reader-that-cannot-see. ∴ ∀ claim about PRESENTATION needs a gate on the PRESENTATION path — a preview tile is ⊥ evidence about it (cf §V627: nor about exposure)|V627,V618,T674
V629: **a gate on a DEFAULTED option ! assert the value EXPLICITLY — "! premultiplied" PASSES on `undefined`, which IS the bug.** `ensurePresentation` passed ⊥ `alphaMode` @ all & vgpu defaults `"premultiplied"`; the T87 comment claimed "opaque is CORRECT here" for months ∴ intent lived ONLY ∈ prose (§V478's shape). ∴ read the value off the `configure()` call actually made & assert it EQUALS the intended one|V478,T674,V461
V630: **ALPHA out of [0,1] @ a SINK is a CATALOGUE-WIDE fault class, & "feedback + additive points" is ⊥ the predicate.** measured across 25 shipped: **10** ship a sink whose alpha leaves [0,1]; E12-Fluid & E31-Corona are CLEAN despite having BOTH feedback & additive points ∴ lead's predicate was wrong. real predicate = **sink alpha leaves [0,1]**, & **goes NEGATIVE** for the flicker. mechanism ⊥ unbounded accumulation but a NEGATIVE-GAIN OSCILLATOR: additive passes floor alpha ≈6.02, Screen's alpha map `L ↦ A+L−A·L` has slope `1−A` = −5.02, feedback 0.62 closes it @ gain **−3.11** (measured −3.13) ∴ `M_{n+1} = 6.02 − 3.112·M_n` reproduces every frame. RGB NEVER flickered (luma flat 0.0485)|T674,B129,B130
V631: **a sink alpha's STEADY STATE = per-frame injection ÷ (1 − persistence) ∴ boundedness is decidable W/O RENDERING.** |gain| < 1 → converges (E29: 0.985 → settles 128, flat f300..f800); |gain| > 1 → diverges, & NEGATIVE gain ALTERNATES SIGN (E9: −3.11 → ±f16max). ∴ `persistence: 0.999` settles @ 1000 & `1.0` genuinely diverges. **& ⊥ extrapolate a trend from a SHORT window** — 12 frames of E29 read as "linear & unbounded" & it was CONVERGING|V630,T679
V632: **a display-transform guard ! be scoped to the DECISION, ⊥ to the SHARED SHADER.** `sinkDisplayTransform` returns `toneMap:"none", encode:false` from **3** branches — a `data` target, a `displayTransform:"none"` measurement dump, & an `-srgb` display sink — & all 3 landed on ONE `OUTPUT_PASSTHROUGH_WGSL`. clamping THERE would have bounded the 2 cases that exist PRECISELY so raw numbers read back (§V516 too-wide guard). ∴ `clampAlpha` is a FIELD on `SinkDisplayTransform`, true only for a DISPLAY sink; `-srgb` gets its own shader|V516,V619,T678
V633: **CHROME THAT ! BE LEGIBLE OVER A LIVE TILE CANNOT LIVE INSIDE THE TILE'S RECT.** ⊥ a z-index bug — STRUCTURAL: `.react-flow__viewport` sets `z-index: 2` on a TRANSFORMED element ∴ it IS a stacking context ∴ EVERY descendant is capped @ 2 whatever number it carries, & `.previewSurface` composites tiles @ 30. ∴ ⊥ local fix exists: lifting the viewport above 30 hole-punches (design note rejects it & it would put EDGES over tiles), & a per-frame screen-space overlay is forbidden by §V111. ∴ the control moves to the node HEADER beside P/B/M — OUTSIDE the composited rect|T675,V487,V111
V634: **`elementFromPoint` is BLIND to a `pointer-events: none` overlay ∴ it is ⊥ a gate for OCCLUSION.** hit testing SKIPS such a surface ∴ it returns the button IDENTICALLY before & after the fix. ⚠ LEAD ERRATUM: lead proposed exactly this gate. ∴ gate occlusion by CONTAINMENT/geometry — is the control a descendant of the rect the tile composites at — & verify red-first by rendering the control BACK inside the slot (did: 3 of 4 red, green on restore). general: **a gate that shares the bug's own blindness cannot see the bug** — cf §V628 (preview tiles force alpha 1) & §V629 (asserting "! premultiplied" passes on undefined)|V461,V628,V629,T675
V635: **⊥ pay for a fix by BLINDING THE INSTRUMENT THAT FOUND THE BUG.** T682 would have made `pixel-probe`'s alpha field & `describe_output`'s `channels.a` read a constant ∴ removing the diagnostic that diagnosed T674, to fix a symptom §B131 shows was ALREADY fixed elsewhere. **& the tell that it was wrong: `presentation-alpha.gpu.test.ts`'s range assertions STILL PASS on a constant 1.0** ∴ the suite stays GREEN while ⊥ longer testing what it NAMES — a gate whose subject has been made constant is a gate that has quietly stopped gating|V461,V628,T682
V636: **E1-Feedback-Echo & E12-Fluid carry STRUCTURED coverage ∈ exported alpha** (corr 0.96–0.99; 97.2% of E1's exported alpha bytes ∈ 0–31 w/ real spread above) while everything else is UNIFORM RESIDUE (`aSD` EXACTLY 0.0000 across 921,600 px) ∴ "sink alpha is meaningless" is FALSE for 2 shipped examples. that distinction is MEASURABLE & ! be re-measured before any change to sink alpha semantics|T682,V630
V637: **a LIVENESS gate ! measure PER-SECOND MAGNITUDE — "does it move at all" passes @ 1/1000 speed.** E35's whole authored motion was invisible ∵ a COEFFICIENT LIED ABOUT ITS UNIT (`ctx.absTime * 0.001`, a ms assumption; **absTime is SECONDS per the manifest**), & it passed EVERY "it changes over time" check ∵ the change was REAL — merely 1000× too slow. same class as T574's half-degree hue, ALSO ∈ this file, ALSO a unit mismatch. ∴ a floor on magnitude-per-second catches both; a floor on mere change catches NEITHER|T683,T574,V624,T521
V638: **a marker reading a CHAOTIC source ! RE-SAMPLE ONLY WHILE INVISIBLE — sample-and-hold, ⊥ smoothing.** if it adopts a new reading WHILE LIT it TELEPORTS, & a chaotic map re-qualifies METRES away by construction ∴ the churn is BIRTHS, ⊥ the tail ∴ every tail remedy fails: position lag makes it WORSE (a lagged marker smears across MORE pixels), lagged rise ~4.5%, longer decay 39.1%→34.7%. gate the RE-ARM on darkness & the relocation happens where ⊥ eye can see it — a display's PHOSPHOR. E34: green energy −92.2%, hard-flip 39.1% → 5.4%, for ONE line|T681,V626,T658
V639: **⊥ STRAIGHTEN a normal to tame a chaotic reflection — the chaos IS the phenomenon.** E34's echoes exist ∵ shallow rays reflect FORWARD off BACK-SLOPES ∴ blending the hit normal toward +Y sends leg 2 into the sky & the echo count goes to **ZERO** @ k=0.55 & k=0.80. a "smoother" input to a physical reading can DELETE the reading ∴ measure the COUNT, ⊥ only the look|T681,V626
V640: **a TWO-SIDED diffuse term has ⊥ BACK SIDE ∴ a BACK LIGHT is ⊥ a RIM — the rim lives ∈ the ENVIRONMENT's FRESNEL term.** `scene-render.wgsl.ts` computes `lambert = abs(dot(N, toLight))` & `highlight = pow(abs(dot(N,H)), gloss)` — two-sided by T301 ∴ a directional light BEHIND the subject lights camera-facing faces EXACTLY as hard as the ones facing away: a back light is a 2nd KEY wearing a rim's name. measured: one @ 1.60 blew the emblem's light half to WHITE & produced ⊥ EDGE. what DOES rim is T632's `envFresnel`, which rises to 1 @ GRAZING where the reflection vector points away from the camera ∴ **the rim is authored as a bright band on the equirect's HORIZON @ (0.5,0.5)** — where a silhouette samples. ⚠ lead's "add a rim light" brief assumed a renderer we ⊥ have|T301,T632,T673 ⟶ **WORKED EXAMPLE & LIMIT, measured (mean |Δ| luma, band-wired vs unwired, split by a 6px erosion of the object mask): GOO frame — ring 45.8, interior 25.9, room 2.8 ∴ 1.8× harder on the OUTLINE = a RIM. EMBLEM frame — ring 14.5, interior 19.5 ∴ STRONGER IN THE BODY = FILL, ⊥ a rim.** ∵ a FLAT disc facing the camera has almost ⊥ GRAZING surface for a Fresnel term to find ∴ **the environment-band rim is a rim ONLY on CURVED geometry & is inherently UNAVAILABLE on the flat camera-facing surface a graphic emblem end WANTS to be** — & flattening the emblem (the fix for "the morph ! read") makes it LESS rimmable. state it as 2 NUMBERS, ⊥ 1 adjective
V641: **a RECORDED look number ! name the COMMIT it was measured at.** T689 exists ∵ E33's md carried absolutes w/ ⊥ provenance ∴ ⊥ way to tell a REGRESSION from a table STALE SINCE AUTHORING w/o bisecting. w/ a commit stamp, drift is DETECTABLE by re-measure & re-taking is MECHANICAL. corollary that saved this pass: **record DELTAS (before/after measured minutes apart on ONE tree) as well as ABSOLUTES** — deltas survive a moved baseline, absolutes do ⊥; & a number computed ANALYTICALLY from a kernel's own arithmetic (E33's silhouette CV) is immune to both|T689,V421,V618,V627
V642: **a look rework claiming to be NET-NEUTRAL ! MEASURE the round trip — "the re-exposure comes home" was APPROXIMATELY true & ⊥ measured-true.** T632 raised E33's exposure & T636 reverted the NUMBERS exactly, so the document is byte-identical — but the PHYSICAL terms that replaced its hand gain left it 22% dimmer, 46% flatter & 36% less motion. reverting a parameter is ⊥ reverting an EFFECT. ∴ ∀ change that swaps a hand-tuned value for a physical term ! re-measure the examples it touches & STATE the delta, ∨ the revert is a claim ⊥ a fact|T689,T632,T636,V637
V643: **look baselines are ASSERTED, ⊥ documentation — §V421 AMENDED (lead approved T689's recommendation).** §V421 as it stood cost a table that went stale ∈ **9 hours** while every gate stayed green, & E24's survived ONLY ∵ its round-3 pass happened to re-measure it. ∴ ONE machine-readable `look-baselines.json` (motion/range/f0max per example) measured by the LIVENESS instrument ∴ §V618 & §V627 baked in BY CONSTRUCTION; gated w/ a modest band; updated DELIBERATELY ∈ the same commit as look-changing work (T645's named-list pattern) ∴ **a moved baseline is a decision someone MADE ON PURPOSE**. md tables then CITE the baseline ∨ carry their measurement commit (§V641), ⊥ freestanding facts. rationale: today's engine moved 3× & nothing had to answer for the pixels|V421,V641,T645,T690
V644: **an ALBEDO map MULTIPLIES ∴ an ADDITIVE contribution through it ! read 1.0 WHERE UNLIT — ∨ the surface goes BLACK.** E34's impact pool splats returns via `renderPoints` into a 512² map feeding the terrain's albedo, offset by a Level w/ black point **−0.1** & white **0** — which is how you say ADD ONE ∈ a multiplying slot. ⚠ the naive version (unlit texels = 0) multiplies the ground to BLACK everywhere the pool ISN'T ∴ the bug looks like "the light broke the terrain" & is really the identity element|T672,V617,V640
V645: **a COMMENT that CONTRADICTS the manifest is a TRAP, ⊥ a typo — it sets the next editor up to repeat the bug.** E30-Nave's kernel says "absTime is frames-since-transport-start"; **absTime is SECONDS**. counterfactual measured: the shipped 0.052 behaves as eye-tuned SECONDS (the ×60 "frames belief" version washes range 0.57→0.36) ∴ the NUMBER is right & the COMMENT is wrong — & an editor who retunes TRUSTING it reproduces §V637's fault exactly. it is the ONLY place ∈ the catalogue contradicting the manifest's stated contract. cf §V478 (intent living only ∈ prose); this is its INVERSE — prose that LIES while the code is correct|V478,V637,T687
V646: **SEED look baselines on a CLEAN tree — a shared tree's UNCOMMITTED work gets baked in.** T690's seed ran while the Obol rebuild sat uncommitted ∴ it captured POST-rebuild values (0.01256/0.5953/0.8834), ⊥ the pre-rebuild ones T689 measured hours earlier (0.00763/0.397/0.5963). it came out CORRECT ONLY ∵ that work landed UNCHANGED minutes later — **a worker who ABANDONED an in-flight look change would have left a baseline for a picture that NEVER SHIPPED**, & every later run would then measure drift AGAINST A FICTION. ∴ a wholesale re-seed ! be done w/ `git status` clean. corollary: 2 measurements of the SAME example minutes apart can BOTH be right & DISAGREE ∴ §V641's commit stamp is what makes them reconcilable|V641,V643,T690,T689
V647: ⚠**`audioPattern` synthesizes band channels LINEAR while the REAL analyser path is dB-DOMAIN (byte over a −100..−30 dB window) ∴ tuning against the pattern fits a floor that is ROUGHLY THE PATTERN'S SILENCE & ROUGHLY MUSIC'S PEAK.** measured on E32: `low` under music mean **0.89** / p01 **0.72**; under pattern mean **0.25** / p01 **0.12**. consequence: `pace1` sits @ 0.48 of a designed 0.18–0.52 & `gnaw1` @ 3.8 of 2–4 **PERMANENTLY** — the parameter has ⊥ dynamic range left ∴ music LOOKS like a constant. **this is a DOMAIN mismatch, ⊥ a taste gap** ∴ ⊥ bias set can satisfy BOTH the offline gate & the owner's ears while it stands|T686,V554,T504,T508
V648: **to tell a DOMAIN fault from a CALIBRATION gap, find the channel that shares the domain & check it PASSES.** `level` is AMPLITUDE on BOTH paths (analyser = time-domain RMS, pattern = sum of linear envelopes) & fits r=**0.893** w/ 45% residual — ~HALF the band channels'. **the 4 dB-domain channels are EXACTLY the 4 that fail.** had the pattern's linearity been a general calibration gap, `level` would fail WITH them ∴ the control is what makes "it is the domain" a MEASUREMENT ⊥ an inference|V647,T700,V461
V649: **a PERCENTAGE ! carry its POPULATION — T671's blink instrument was measuring 23 PIXELS.** "nucleus thresholded @ display 205" selects **23 px @ frame 900** under the pattern (155 @ f300) ∴ a hard-flip rate quoted to 2 decimals (23.28% → 18.68%) over 23 samples is NOISE wearing precision. under MUSIC the same threshold selects 2,320–3,342 px ∴ **the 2 rounds were never comparable POPULATIONS** & the improvement they recorded is ⊥ refutable ∨ confirmable. ∴ report the N w/ the %, & when a threshold's population moves w/ the ARM, the metric is ⊥ a metric — use a frame-wide ∨ fixed-region measure instead|T671,T686,V461,V641
V650: **AGREEMENT BETWEEN TWO ZEROS IS ⊥ AGREEMENT — a cross-check case ! PROVE IT CARRIES SIGNAL before its agreement counts.** T702: for a TONE, 3 of 4 bands are legitimately **0.0000** ∴ an all-zero browser reading would have matched an all-zero model & looked GREEN, confirming nothing. ∴ ∀ case ∈ a model-vs-reality gate ! assert NON-TRIVIAL content first. this is §V461's shape ∈ its most seductive form: the gate PASSES, the numbers MATCH, & ⊥ claim was tested|V461,V498,T702
V651: **a BAND-AVERAGE instrument UNDER-READS a NARROWBAND signal — DILUTION, ⊥ refutation.** T702's 1st shape assertion used a 60 Hz TONE & measured steps **0.072–0.124** against the predicted 0.143; the tone occupies ONE bin of `low`'s TEN while the other nine sit pinned on the floor rail ∴ the AVERAGE grows slower than the MAPPING does. BROADBAND fills every bin & leaves only the transfer curve. ∴ measure a band's transfer w/ a signal that OCCUPIES the band; & keep the tone case w/ its reason recorded, so a reader measuring 0.10 where the arithmetic says 0.14 FINDS the explanation ⊥ rediscovers it|T702,V650
V652: **choose the §V620 suite list by WHAT THE CHANGE CAN BREAK, ⊥ by habit.** `e3f39dc` changed a VALUE NODE's OUTPUT DOMAIN & ran audio 15/15 + value-mute-bypass 60/60 + typecheck — all green, all irrelevant to the damage. **`liveness.test.ts` reddens on exactly that commit (5 failed | 28 passed vs 33/33 @ parent)** ∴ ONE run would have caught 5 broken examples BEFORE the owner did. ∴ a commit touching a value node's output domain ! run liveness; more generally the suite list is an ARGUMENT about blast radius, ⊥ a ritual|V620,T703,T701
V653: **a GREEN look baseline means "the picture still looks about the same" — it does ⊥ mean "this example was UNAFFECTED".** E30-Nave: `roll1.value1 ← bore1:low` went from a FLAT CONSTANT 0.000 to a live **0.088..0.289** swing — a DEAD parameter came ALIVE — yet motion moved −6.2% & range −5.7%, INSIDE the 10%/0.003 band ∴ green. 6 audioPattern examples, **5 caught, 1 MISSED**. ⊥ a hole ∈ the gate's construction — a LIMIT on what a green row LICENSES you to conclude. ∴ ⊥ cite a green baseline as evidence a SEMANTIC change did ⊥ reach an example|V643,T703,V649
V654: ⚠**§V471's CALIBRATION BAR WAS NEVER VALIDATED AGAINST MUSIC — E31-Corona's OFFLINE PICTURE HAD BEEN LYING.** the bar did ⊥ MOVE w/ T701: under a REAL track Corona's `coat1.scale` was **ALREADY ~2.0** (`grade1 = 0.55 + 2.6·highMid`, music highMid ≈ 0.56) while the linear pattern showed 0.818–0.928. T547's headroom retune was judged OFFLINE against that pattern ∴ **the standard every other example is judged by has never been what the owner SEES w/ music playing.** ∴ Corona needs its own round & it is the FIRST to be judged against a truthful pattern; ⊥ cite §V471 as settled until then|V471,T701,T547,V647 ⚠**AMENDED by a 2nd, INDEPENDENT measurement — the claim as first filed was TOO STRONG.** the retuning worker re-measured & EYEBALLED E31 post-retune: **character INTACT** — corona, white-hot crests, magenta body, palette breathing, all present. ∴ **Corona was ⊥ MISTUNED AS A PICTURE**; its offline NUMBERS shift (motion +21%, 0.065→0.078) ∵ a strike now decays LINEARLY ∈ dB & carries longer @ the top — a TIME-PROFILE change, ⊥ a look change. **what SURVIVES of this row: the offline picture was never VALIDATED against music, & the parameter VALUES differed ~2× between pattern & track.** what does ⊥ survive: that the bar itself is unreliable. ∴ §V471 STANDS; Corona still earns its own round as the 1st judged against a truthful pattern
V655: **a FINITENESS check CANNOT SEE a DEGENERATE BASIS — zero is perfectly finite.** T706's gate, 1st draft: "every matrix entry is finite" **PASSED w/ the guard DELETED**, ∵ `cross([0,1,0],[0,1,0]) = 0` produces a matrix of entirely finite zeros. caught by the agent's OWN red-verify, ⊥ by review. ∴ assert the PROPERTY THE THING IS FOR — the shipped version asserts SEPARATION OF 2 GROUND POINTS ON SCREEN — ⊥ a numerical health check that a collapse satisfies. same family as §V634 (a gate sharing the bug's blindness) & §V650 (agreement between 2 zeros)|V461,V634,V650,T706 ⚠**5th instance, T705**: that agent's OWN first gate draft asserted window + title + host-present — **the exact broken state the owner reported** — & was replaced by asserting a NEW canvas w/ `ownerDocument === child` actually PRESENTED. the family now: §V634 (elementFromPoint blind to the overlay), §V650 (two zeros agreeing), §V655 (finite zeros), §V656 (right count, wrong order), & this
V656: **a COUNT-ONLY assertion passes a REPLACEMENT THAT WIRES WRONG.** T695: w/o insert semantics a drop-replace still counts right — **3 edges in, 3 edges out** — & lands at the END instead of in the replaced slot. the count reading is TRUE & the wiring is WRONG ∴ gate the ORDER, ⊥ the cardinality; red-first on exactly that (count-only passes while order is wrong). 4th member of the family w/ §V634, §V650, §V655|V461,V655,T695
V657: **a test ! MEASURE ITS TARGET AT THE MOMENT OF THE ACTION — ⊥ before it**, when the action itself MOVES the target. e2e `connect()` measured before the press while React Flow AUTO-PANS mid-connection ∴ harmless on a 1-input node & DECISIVE on sockets **16 px** apart — a drop aimed @ `in2#1` arrived as `in2#2` ∴ every drop-replace assertion would have been meaningless WHILE GREEN. fix: wait for React Flow's own `connectingto` & REFUSE to release when it cannot tell which socket it is over — a refusal that immediately exposed a latent ambiguity ∈ `shader-errors.spec.ts`. & `fitAll` now waits for the viewport transform to STOP, which fixed a pre-existing `project-io` FLAKE|V461,V649,T695
V658: **a `ResizeObserver` BELONGS TO THE WINDOW THAT MADE IT ∴ it survives a cross-document move as a DEAD observer.** T705 layer one: the DOCK's observer fired ONCE mid-detach — `clientWidth` 0 → a **1×1 backing store** → the owner's "empty page" — & never fired again. ∴ ∀ per-window resource attached to a MOVABLE element (observers, contexts, media, timers keyed to a document) ! be RE-ARMED per element after adoption, ⊥ carried|V96,T705,V659
V659: **a WebGPU canvas that was CONFIGURED & then ADOPTED cross-document is PERMANENTLY INERT — & it LIES about it.** T705 layer two, measured AFTER fixing layer one: full size, `getContext` still answering, **0.0 mean luma, forever**. ⊥ error, ⊥ exception, ⊥ refusal you can read. **the ONLY escape is a FRESH ELEMENT** — which the float-THEN-load path had accidentally proven by working. ∴ key the canvas on an adoption epoch so React remounts it; & ⊥ trust `getContext` answering as evidence a context is ALIVE|T705,V658,V628
V660: **guard a DEGENERATE state @ the WRITE path too, ⊥ only the READ.** a read-time guard makes the state SURVIVABLE; a write-time guard makes it UNAUTHORABLE. T706 guards the pole at read (`|d.y| > 0.999 → alternate up`); T692's gizmo ALSO clamps elevation off the poles when WRITING ∴ the document can never HOLD the pose. ∴ a value a UI can author ! be constrained where it is AUTHORED — a downstream guard silently corrects a document that reads as broken to anyone inspecting it|T706,T692,V655
V661: **a control ! ⊥ APPEAR where it CANNOT WORK.** T692: a DRIVEN camera offers ⊥ gizmo — `readPose` refuses mode envelopes ∴ a drag can never clobber a driven binding w/ a plain value. offering a disabled ∨ silently-failing control would be an affordance that LIES (§T639(a)); REFUSING to draw it is honest & needs ⊥ explanation. cf T669: absence reads as a CONSEQUENCE when the tile already says WHY|T669,T639,T692,V90
V662: **a frame-mode branch ! be written `mode !== "realtime"`, ⊥ `mode === "offline"`.** `mode` is THREE-valued (`realtime|fixed-step|offline`) & **the headless harness runs `fixed-step` while the cook oracle runs `offline`** ∴ an `=== "offline"` branch leaves EVERY GATE on the wrong path — silently plausible, silently green, §T650/§T655's failure exactly. & phrased as "is this a REAL-TIME presentation?" a mode added LATER blocks BY DEFAULT, which is the safe direction. general: **negate against the ONE mode you know, ⊥ enumerate the ones you happen to remember**|T715,T650,T655,V461
V663: **a report ! MARK PROVENANCE PER CLAIM — "I read this" vs "I was told this" vs "I infer this" — & an agent ! ⊥ REPORT A SUBAGENT'S FINDINGS IT NEVER RECEIVED.** §B138: a survey mixing verified & unverified claims INDISTINGUISHABLY is UNUSABLE even where its conclusions are RIGHT, ∵ a reader cannot tell which half to build on — & the lead recorded 2 fabricated citations into SPEC before the correction. ∴ (a) a pending subagent's result is ⊥ knowledge until it ARRIVES; (b) cite ⊥ path ∨ line you have ⊥ opened; (c) when a report is mixed, PUBLISH THE SPLIT — this agent's own retraction is the model: read-directly / checked-after / false. corollary for the LEAD: a citation is CHEAP TO VERIFY & a wrong one poisons the row FOREVER ∴ spot-check paths before recording an erratum|B138,V620,V641
V664: **a READ-SIDE REPAIR that "fixes" data by DROPPING it can silently ERASE a feature's persistence.** T705(b): the v3 layout projection's repair drops a floating entry ALREADY SEEN ∈ a zone — correct under v3's EXCLUSIVE semantics & FATAL once a tab is deliberately ∈ BOTH lists ∴ the persisted floating list emptied itself on every load until the projection was taught the difference. ∴ ∀ normalizer/repair ! be re-read when a data model gains a DELIBERATE duplicate; & a "repair" that discards is a WRITE wearing a read's clothes. sibling trap same pass: `allTabs` had to DEDUPE ∵ a floated tab is now ∈ 2 lists & content ! render ONCE|T705,V96,T590
V665: **a NAMESPACE PREFIX consumed by a WILDCARD WALKER ! be gated, ⊥ assumed distinct.** `registerSyntheticMediaSources` claims EVERY `media:`-prefixed external texture & registers a test card ∴ an inference result keyed `media:` would silently render **diagonal test-card bars ∈ every Dawn gate** — plausible, green, wrong. ∴ `infer:` + **a test asserting the namespaces stay apart**. general: when a harness fakes a whole PREFIX, the prefix is an INTERFACE & a new producer joining it inherits the fake|T715,T650,V461
V666: **a GREEN gate is ⊥ evidence until a MUTATION REDDENS IT — & reddens IT ALONE.** §V461 asks that a gate CAN fail; this asks that it fails for the RIGHT REASON & that its neighbours do ⊥. T715 Phase 0 shipped 4 mutations, each reddening its OWN test & nothing else, then reverted: `settle` skipping in-flight; never-yet returning `undefined`; the predicate flipped to `mode === "offline"`; the `inFlight` guard dropped. that is SPECIFICITY, ⊥ merely sensitivity — & it is what the 5 blind gates of §V655 would all have failed|V461,V655,T715
V667: **a CROSS-CUTTING TYPE change (a new port kind, a new enum member) reddens EVERY consumer until ALL are updated ∴ ∈ a SHARED tree it ! be done in ONE push, ⊥ incrementally.** T704's `projector` port kind mid-thread left **9 typecheck errors** across `ports.ts`, `port-compat.ts`, `reference-lines.tsx`, `search.ts`, `ui/ports.ts` & a test ∴ **⊥ other worker could claim a green typecheck**, & 3 stopped to prove the errors were ⊥ theirs. an exhaustive `switch` ∨ `satisfies Record<Kind,…>` is a FEATURE (§T675 made a new payload kind a typecheck failure ON PURPOSE) — & the SAME property makes the intermediate state EXPENSIVE for everyone else. ∴ thread it in one sitting, ∨ work it ∈ a worktree & land it whole|V479,B123,T675,T704
V668: **FADING an ADDITIVE thing hides it; FADING an OPAQUE thing PAINTS BLACK.** T711: a beam is opaque scene geometry ∴ the lead's "fade the misses out at max range" would have drawn a **BLACK RIBBON over lit terrain**, ⊥ nothing. ∴ before dimming ANYTHING to hide it, ask which BLEND it draws through — for an opaque primitive the only honest hide is **⊥ DRAWING IT**. corollary measured same pass: recolouring a MISS class blinks worse than the hit class it replaces (0.4% → 11.3% churn) ∵ the CLASS BOUNDARY itself is what oscillates ∴ ⊥ recolour a binary verdict, DROP it|T711,T681,V638,V644
V669: **a gate on a BOUNDARY ! assert the BOUNDARY'S SHAPE — a downstream PIXEL check can be MASKED by ordering, defaulting ∨ OVERWRITE.** §V666 caught its own author: the §V665 namespace test **did ⊥ redden** when the prefix guard was reverted entirely, ∵ `registerMediaSource` **REPLACES on re-register** & the inference feed runs SECOND ∴ a media card wrongly claiming an `infer:` texture is silently OVERWRITTEN a moment later. the bug was real, the guard was right, & the pixel test **passed for a reason unrelated to what it claimed to assert**. ∴ replaced w/ a direct gate on WHICH SOURCE IDS EACH FEED CLAIMS (fake backend recording them), reddening in BOTH directions. general: test the CONTRACT AT THE SEAM, ⊥ its consequence 3 layers downstream|V666,V665,V655,T715
V670: **RELEASING a windowed file means COMMITTING your change — ⊥ merely CEASING TO EDIT.** T710 handed back `documents.ts` w/ its 465-line E13 hunk & its `look-baselines.json` row still UNCOMMITTED while it moved on to the md & tests ∴ the next holder (T711) could ⊥ `git commit -- <paths>` w/o **landing another worker's in-flight rebuild on their behalf** — §B133's exact hazard, & the §V494 pathspec rule forbids the index-staging workaround. ∴ a window CLOSES w/ a commit; if follow-up files remain, commit the WINDOWED file & continue outside it. corollary: a worker holding uncommitted edits ∈ a CONTESTED file blocks EVERY successor, ⊥ just the file|V494,B133,V643,T710,T711
V671: **a NEGATIVE result requires a PASSING CONTROL — a broken instrument reporting "absent" is INDISTINGUISHABLE from a real absence.** T715's 1st WebNN probe returned `navigator.gpu: undefined` from Playwright's Chromium ∈ ALL 3 configs INCLUDING headed w/ `--enable-unsafe-webgpu` — & **we KNOW WebGPU works ∵ the app runs on it** ∴ the CONTROL FAILED ∴ the negative was ⊥ evidence & the agent nearly reported it. re-run ∈ real Chrome 151 w/ the control PASSING (`navigator.gpu` object, adapter vendor `apple`, architecture `metal-3`): **`navigator.ml` = `undefined`** ∴ **WebNN is ⊥ PRESENT on the owner's machine — ⊥ flag-off-but-detectable, the ENTRY POINT does ⊥ EXIST.** ∴ ∀ "X is unavailable" claim ! carry a sibling "Y IS available" measured the SAME WAY|V461,V650,T715,T381
V672: **a capability label ! be LICENSED BY USE, ⊥ by SELECTION — & PAIRING the name w/ a MEASURED NUMBER makes it unable to lie about SPEED even where it cannot see the DEVICE.** @ detection time a path is CHOSEN but ⊥ TAKEN ∴ a bare "WebGPU" claims a path ⊥ yet exercised & "WebGPU · — ms" is a label w/ its evidence MISSING. ∴ the backend label appears ONLY after a completed inference; before that the node reports its STATE ("Acquiring model — 142 MB of 380 MB" | "Waiting for first result" | "Model unavailable — showing a flat depth map"). **self-correcting property**: ask transformers.js for `webnn-npu`, let it silently fall back INSIDE WebNN, & the label "WebNN" stays TRUE (we DID take that path) while **the LATENCY exposes the fallback**|V469,T715,T381
V673: **`memo` does ⊥ protect against CONTEXT — a context value re-renders EVERY consumer straight THROUGH `memo`.** T714: `NodeView` was memoized, its payload deliberately `{nodeId}`, & its projection reference-stable — all correct, all useless, ∵ it ALSO called `useGraphCanvas()`. ∴ **a memoized component's real dependency set is its props PLUS every context it reads**, & a context value rebuilt per revision defeats the whole memo strategy silently — the code looks right & the property is untrue (§V480's shape, one level up). ∴ ∀ context value shared by many consumers ! be reference-stable per member: read mutable state through a REF, & keep a derived collection's object when its MEMBERSHIP does ⊥ move|V480,T519,T714
V674: **a COUNTING gate ! subscribe to EXACTLY what the real component subscribes to.** T714's wrapper is `memo`'d **AND** calls `useGraphCanvas()` ∴ it re-renders under the 2 conditions `NodeView` does — **a wrapper that skipped the context would go QUIET during the very failure it exists to catch**. & it counts the thing that SCALES: renders on a 6-node vs a 60-node graph, asserting the DIFFERENCE does ⊥ grow (red-first **305 vs 35** = N+1 per edit, visible ∈ the numbers; after **0 and 0**), ⊥ a wall-clock threshold generous enough to survive noise & therefore generous enough to survive the regression returning|V666,V669,V649,T714
V675: **a feedback loop closing on the FINISHED FRAME smears EVERYTHING the frame contains ∴ a SELECTIVE trail closes on a SIDE BRANCH composited back.** E34 is the catalogue's 1st SELECTIVE loop (a luminance THRESHOLD decides what ENTERS it) & the 1st that does ⊥ close the way §V471.5 describes: it closes on `smear1`, a side branch added into the bloom's composite, ∵ closing on the output would trail the terrain, the chrome & the beams alike. ∴ **§V471.5 describes the DEFAULT, ⊥ the only shape** — & the roster ∈ `temporal.test.ts` is an EXPLICIT list, so adding a loop REDDENS it BY DESIGN (the gate working, ⊥ a sweep)|V471,T711,V631
V676: **an EXEMPTION silences a gate ∴ use one only when the GATE is wrong, NEVER when the PROSE is.** T716's md named `materialUnlit` ∈ a table describing a MUTATION, & E33's graph genuinely lacks the type ∴ a `DELIBERATE` entry would be **a gate declining to check a TRUE claim** — the prose gets rephrased instead. corollary from the same pass: when a rebuilt example inherits a measured table from the OLD form, **KEEP it w/ its ORIGINAL commit stamp & say WHAT it was measured on** — re-deriving produces a 3rd set of numbers for ONE invariant & makes the record worse, ⊥ better (§V641's stamp is what makes that legible)|V641,V643,T716,V640
V677: **⊥ MUTATE A SHARED SOURCE FILE TO TEST — mutate the GENERATED ARTIFACT the gate actually READS, & RESTORE BY REGENERATING.** T711's 1st mutation attempt was a `perl -i` on `documents.ts` **while 2 other workers had live hunks in it**, & it was a NO-OP BY LUCK: a shell expansion ate `${LIDAR_RANGE}` from BOTH pattern & replacement ∴ it substituted a string matching nothing. had it matched, it would have written into a contended file. **∴ the safe form is also the BETTER INSTRUMENT**: these gates read the `examples/` DIRECTORY via `listExamples()`, ⊥ the source ∴ mutating the SHIPPED `.loom.json` hits EXACTLY the surface the gates see & never touches a contended file. **restore is the GENERATOR, never a checkout** (§GOD-RULE). verify the tree clean after each pass|V666,V494,B133,T711 ⟶ **STRONGER FORM, used by T721: an ISOLATED `git worktree` — files copied in, `node_modules` symlinked, mutated THERE, worktree removed.** it needs ⊥ discipline about who else is typing & **the shared tree is never WRITTEN AT ALL** ∴ prefer it for SOURCE-level mutation; mutate-the-generated-artifact stays right for gates that read `examples/`
V678: **§V653 DEMONSTRATED, ⊥ argued: `liveness.test.ts` stayed GREEN under ALL TEN deliberate breakages** — including every ray drawn to full range, & 240 bounce legs (the green-spaghetti frame). @ 192×108 w/ a 10% band a look baseline **does ⊥ see structural damage this large** ∴ **a green baseline row means "about the same picture", ⊥ "this example is intact" — it is ⊥ a STRUCTURE gate & ⊥ cite it as one.** the claims are what catch structure; the baseline catches DRIFT|V653,V643,V666,T711
V681: **⊥ STILL-FRAME instrument can see MOTION damage — & most of ours are still-frame.** T716's most informative mutation (`z = 1 − 2u` → an INDEPENDENT sphere direction) **renders a PIXEL-IDENTICAL still frame** & re-deals EVERY tile in motion; ONLY the claim that names the correspondence sees it — ⊥ the rendered legibility gate, ⊥ the baseline, nothing else. same class as §V678's ten breakages surviving `liveness`. ∴ a property about CORRESPONDENCE ACROSS FRAMES (a tile keeping its identity, a marker holding its place, a beam matching its mark) ! be asserted STRUCTURALLY ∨ across FRAME PAIRS — a single rendered frame is evidence about a MOMENT, ⊥ about a MOTION|V678,V653,V666,T716,T711
